manifest.name: dsh-math-copy
manifest.description: Copy rendered math in the DSH Web UI as its LaTeX source instead of KaTeX's glyph text.

bundle.text:
# dsh-math-copy — the bundle's own patch layer.
#
# One Loader entry gives the package a home in the profile; the browser half is
# picked up through `dsh.client` in package.json, exactly like the shipped
# ui-* packages (no per-plugin wiring).
#
# Settings: the host half declares three volatile fields, so the Settings
# transport serves them under this row's id (`math-copy`) and the browser half
# renders the form on this bundle's row in the Plugins page (its own panel is
# registered into the `plugins.row.config` slot). Values written there are
# persisted into the active profile's Cordis patch, like any other plugin form.
#
# The defaults live in index.js (schema) and client.js (behavior) and are only
# used until a value is saved; a hand-written `config:` here overrides them and
# will be shown in the form.
- insert:
    - id: math-copy
      name: 'dsh-math-copy'

readme.text:
English | [中文](README.zh.md)

Copying rendered math from the DSH Web UI puts the formula's **LaTeX source** on
the clipboard, instead of KaTeX's visual glyph text (`x2` for `x^2`).
The Web UI renders math with KaTeX, and KaTeX keeps the original TeX source in the formula's accessibility subtree: ```html …\frac{a}{b}… …glyphs…

The browser's own selection copy walks the visible layout (and the clipped MathML
arm), so it produces glyph text. This plugin listens for `copy` on the document;
when the selection intersects at least one formula it marks those formulas,
clones the selection, swaps each formula for its TeX wrapped in math delimiters,
writes `text/plain` (and `text/html`) and cancels the default action. A copy
whose selection holds no math is left completely alone.
Selecting half a formula still yields the whole formula's TeX.

Three fields, editable in the Plugins page:

| field | default | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inline formula delimiter | `"$"` | wrapped around inline math (empty → bare TeX) |
| Display formula delimiter | `"$$"` | wrapped around display math (empty → bare TeX) |
| Also replace the rich-text flavor | `true` | substitute math in the `text/html` flavor too; off keeps the untouched selection markup for rich paste targets |

- `index.js` declares the fields on `export const Config` and marks each one
  `.volatile()`. Only volatile fields are projected into a form: the settings
  service serves them under this entry's profile row id, `math-copy`.
- `client.js` subscribes to that form through `ctx.configForms.get("math-copy")`
  (the same way the shipped `ui-chat` reads its preferences) and folds it over
  its own defaults, so the copy handler always reads the current values.
- The panel is registered into the `plugins.row.config` slot with the key
  `<package name>#<row id>` (`dsh-math-copy#math-copy`). No shipped client
  renders settings forms automatically, so the plugin renders its own.

Find it at **插件 (Plugins) → dsh-math-copy → the `math-copy` row → its
configuration block**. Writes go through the settings transport and are
persisted into the active profile's Cordis patch, so they survive restarts.

Changing the host half (`index.js`) needs a **DSH restart**: the host module
generation is cached for the process lifetime, and the profile's HMR entry runs
with `root: []` (no source watching). Client-only edits (`client.js`) reach the
page on a reload.

```

Reload the Web UI page afterwards so the new client bundle enters the boot graph.

Restarting DSH after a host-half change is required — the host module generation
is cached for the process lifetime.

Developed and verified against **dsh core 0.2.0-rc.2** (DSH Desktop
2.0.15-beta.1). No `engines.dsh` range is declared yet: the plugin uses
long-standing client services (`slots`, `locale`, `configForms`, `ctx.inject`),
but only this version has actually been run, and a range that admits prerelease
builds has to name each `major.minor.patch` tuple explicitly. Declare one once
another version has been tested.

`tools/asar-extract.mjs` reads Electron's `app.asar` (list or extract by path
substring) — used to read the shipped client code that renders markdown and math:

```sh
node tools/asar-extract.mjs "/Applications/DeepSeek Harness.app/Contents/Resources/app.asar" list katex
node tools/asar-extract.mjs "/Applications/DeepSeek Harness.app/Contents/Resources/app.asar" extract dsh-client-ui-primitives /tmp/dshx
```

`index.js` resolves `@deepseek-ai/schemastery` through the active profile when
the direct specifier misses (a directory-installed bundle is linked into the
profile, so Node resolves its imports from the workspace instead). Without the
schema the plugin still copies with its built-in defaults; only the form is
missing. A normally installed copy (npm or GitHub, which is what
`dshmarket` performs) resolves the direct specifier and never reaches the
fallback.
